newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest shares mixed, market back to normal.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest shares mixed, market back to normal.

text.p: Bucharest stocks traded mixed on Friday in what brokers said was moderate interest ahead of the weekend and after two record turnover highs this week.
"There was no special to lead volumes and turnover high, the way it happened on Wednesday and Thursday," said a broker.

Volume was 3.2 million shares on turnover of 11.6 billion lei. Turnover the previous day had soared to a record 65.5 billion from an all-time high of 25.9 billion on Wednesday thanks to special deals in first-tier chemical plant Oltchim and Azomures fertiliser maker.
"The market returned to normal and Azomures and Oltchim gained ground after artificial losses due to special deals on Thursday," a trader said.
Brokers said foreigners, responsible for the special trades the previous day, continued to buy into the two heavyweights.

Azomures closed 1,100 lei stronger at 3,600. On Thursday, its closing quote was brought by the special deals which, due to the high volumes involved, were struck at a lower price. Thursday's best market bid for Azomures was 3,450 lei.
Oltchim gained 1,250 lei on Friday to 3,350. Its lower close the previous day was also triggered by special deals.

Two independent indices, the VAB and the BIG, climbed 17.6 and 24.19 percent respectively from Thursday, with the BIG hitting a record high, mainly thanks to the reinvigoration of Azomures and Oltchim.
The other gainer on the first tier was Antibiotice pharmaceuticals which saw a seven percent rise in its average price to 5,963 and closed 500 lei firmer at 6,400.
Arctic refrigerator maker and pharmaceuticals firm Terapia lost 50 lei each to end at 3,050 and 6,450, while fertiliser maker Sofert SOFE.BX shed 9,500 lei to 28,500.
Compa COPA.BX vehicle parts maker, this week's newcomer, had one deal in some 4,400 shares at 2,150 lei per share.
Brokers said they expected rises in most stocks early next week, with a correction getting hold of the market later.
The leader on the second tier was Policolor dye maker, with some 184,000 shares changing hands on turnover of around one billion lei. It closed 100 lei higher at 5,900.
